question: After providing a slow synaptic reference, can a shared, reward-trained local rule learn when and where to use it, and can it transfer to independently trained bodies?
physical_rule: Use the previously calibrated slow update beta=.02. Each receiver has one restoration gain. A scalar comparator learns a constant logit. The adaptive comparator learns the same intercept plus three shared coefficients multiplying the receiver's post-taste activity, change from contact to taste, and mean magnitude of current incoming deviations from its slow reference. All fast writes, growth and retirement continue. No private labels, question IDs, object addresses, timestamps, prediction errors from the evaluator or externally computed utility enter the gain.
fit: Three independent searches. In each, both arms start at gamma=.12, use identical episodes and equal numbers of perturbations. Paired antithetic perturbations update 1 versus 4 coefficients from only the earned resource on one uniformly sampled final A, B or X motor action. The graph actually tastes A, B, intervening objects, and then X. No evolutionary reward sums three hypothetical branches. Training draws from original 731–736; the rule is shared across all six and is tested on new 811–816 without refit. One or four initial exposures, recurring or absent A, and 4/8/16/32 intervening events. Stop at 2048 updates; intermediate scores have no role in choosing the endpoint.
final: Primary matched evaluation on independent births and worlds: after four initial exposures, A absent for 16, 64 or 128 contacts, and one X experience, fork A/B/X before any new feedback. Report each probability, joint actual success and adaptive minus equal-budget fitted constant. Compare spatially permuted gains and a per-lane mean-gain dose control. Show three external search seeds separately and pair differences before resampling; never count them as new training births.
scope: This is a small, external meta-optimization of an added stabilization rule. The living graph gets only its physical state and taste. Evidence of any advantageous spatial control requires both functional improvement and the matched location interventions.
